## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Biological age uncertainty identified as novel healthspan predictor** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.26.26364091)
  - A probabilistic framework applied to over 450,000 UK Biobank participants across NMR metabolomic, plasma proteomic, and blood test profiles established Biological Age Uncertainty (BAU) from the width of predicted-age distributions.
  - Higher BAU independently predicted mortality (hazard ratios of 1.24 for NMR and 1.40 for proteomic BAU per standard deviation) and multimorbidity beyond standard biological age gap metrics.
  - Genetic and physiological analyses linked elevated BAU to multi-organ discordant aging, chronic inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and tissue remodeling.

- **Repetitive negative thinking linked to longitudinal amyloid accumulation** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366526)
  - Longitudinal neuroimaging in 94 cognitively healthy adults demonstrated that repetitive negative thinking (RNT) significantly predicted increased global cortical amyloid deposition over 3 years (p = 0.012, Florbetapir-PET).
  - Voxelwise analysis localized amyloid accumulation to early Alzheimer's disease-vulnerable regions, including the precuneus, posterior cingulate cortex, and medial frontal cortex.
  - RNT associations remained significant after controlling for anxiety and depressive symptoms, while no changes were observed in FDG-PET glucose metabolism or volumetric brain atrophy.

- **Burn wound excision drives acute hypermetabolic response in preclinical models** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.26.761985)
  - A controlled mouse model evaluating ~15% body surface area scald burns revealed that surgical wound excision increased resting energy expenditure (REE) by 102%–136% during the first week post-injury compared to controls.
  - Excision (alone or combined with scald burn) resulted in significantly greater acute body mass loss, cachexia, and bone mineral density reduction than burn injury alone.
  - Results indicate that rodent models must incorporate burn wound excision to accurately model clinical hypermetabolism and cachectic responses.

- **Epigenetic methylation score tracks lifetime depression exposure** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366842)
  - Evaluation of a 15-site blood DNA methylation score (MD-MS) in 731 NESDA cohort participants showed significantly higher MD-MS levels in individuals with lifetime major depressive disorder (p = 0.012) and chronic depression trajectories over 6 years (p = 0.001).
  - MD-MS positively correlated with inflammatory (C-reactive protein) and metabolic biomarkers (triglycerides, fasting glucose).
  - Adjustment for psychosocial variables (childhood trauma, social activity) attenuated the association between MD-MS and lifetime depression by 17.5%.

- **Slide-level attention CNNs benchmarked for serous ovarian carcinoma grading** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.21.26351441)
  - A leakage-controlled evaluation on 259 whole-slide images (UBC-OCEAN cohort) demonstrated that an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNet with differential attention achieved an AUC of 0.862 in differentiating high-grade from low-grade serous carcinoma.
  - The pretrained MobileNet significantly outperformed no-attention baselines and the Phikon pathology foundation model benchmark (AUC 0.834).
  - Adding spatial attention branches to channel attention produced no detectable performance gain (AUC 0.824 to 0.822), highlighting the critical role of transfer learning over spatial module complexity.

- **Machine learning detects chronic kidney disease from routine full blood counts** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.27.26366677)
  - Evaluation of 155 patient records from a Ghanaian hospital demonstrated that ML models using 8 raw full blood count (FBC) parameters plus age detected CKD with 83.9% accuracy and an AUC of 0.939 when synthetic oversampling (SMOTE) was applied prior to splitting.
  - Restricting resampling to training folds yielded a held-out testing accuracy of 61.5% and an AUC of 0.604 across 39 unseen patients, highlighting a 22.4 percentage-point performance shift based on preprocessing design.

- **Rapid 6-hour direct-from-urine assay triages suspected urinary tract infections** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366819)
  - A prospective diagnostic accuracy study (n=120) evaluating SIBURI/SIBURI+ (nitrate-reduction and bromothymol blue broths) demonstrated 92.7% sensitivity, 92.4% specificity, and a 96.1% negative predictive value against quantitative urine culture.
  - SIBURI alone identified 70.7% of culture-positive specimens, while SIBURI+ detected non-nitrate-reducing pathogens including enterococci, streptococci, *Acinetobacter*, and *Candida*.

- **Targeting TEAD in Hippo signaling for small-molecule inhibitor discovery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42966706/)
  - Structure-based drug discovery identified novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting TEAD transcription factors to modulate Hippo pathway signaling.

- **Targeting SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein phase separation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42966466/)
  - A structure-based drug discovery approach identified small-molecule phase separation modulators targeting the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein.

- **Novel furan-chalcone derivatives target bacterial DNA gyrase and Topoisomerase IV** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42965901/)
  - Design, synthesis, and *in silico* modeling identified novel furan-chalcone derivatives exhibiting dual-targeting activity against bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **PROgnostic SIgnatures evaluate stage II colon cancer outcomes in Phase III TOSCA trial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42966319/)
  - The PROSIT study evaluated prognostic gene signatures in stage II colon cancer patients enrolled in the Phase III TOSCA trial to refine post-surgical risk stratification and treatment selection.

- **Extended outcomes reported for ADAPT AF-DES trial** [New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2612608?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  - Extended clinical follow-up outcomes were reported for the ADAPT AF-DES trial, examining long-term antithrombotic management strategies in patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing drug-eluting stent percutaneous coronary intervention.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **FDA regulatory decision calendar highlighted for November PDUFA dates** [BioStocks via X](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2116523081984266390)
  - Unconfirmed market tracking highlights upcoming November FDA PDUFA decision dates for several biopharma companies, including Agios ($AGIO), NRx Pharmaceuticals ($NRXP), Cytokinetics ($CYTK), Summit Therapeutics ($SMMT), Savara ($SVRA), Capricor ($CAPR), BridgeBio ($BBIO), Pyros ($PYPD), Cogent Biosciences ($COGT), and Vertex ($VRTX).

- **FDA updates GDUFA paid facilities list for generic drug manufacturing** [U.S. FDA](http://www.fda.gov/industry/generic-drug-user-fee-amendments/gdufa-paid-facilities-list)
  - The FDA released its updated Generic Drug User Fee Amendments (GDUFA) facility payment tracking list, detailing user fee compliance for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API), finished dosage form (FDF), and contract manufacturing organization (CMO) sites.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Biotech]** **Anthropic hires Atlas Venture partner following AI-driven drug discovery collaboration** [Prof_Oak_ via X](https://x.com/Prof_Oak_/status/2116546309494620318)
  - AI developer Anthropic hired Cody Schultz from Atlas Venture portfolio biotech Mithril, emphasizing the application of AI workflows to virtual drug discovery operations and operational capital efficiency.

## Public Health & Policy

- **High-frequency neuroprotective prescribing persists despite physician knowledge gaps in China** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366879)
  - A nationwide survey of 1,982 neurologists in China found that 80.5% reported high-frequency neuroprotective agent prescribing (treating ≥60% of acute ischemic stroke patients).
  - High-frequency prescribing coexisted with lower self-rated familiarity in 37.5% of respondents; prescribing was strongly associated with perceived treatment importance (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.29) and high benefit expectations (aPR 1.20).

- **Surveillance reveals high fluoroquinolone resistance in Canadian long-term care facilities** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366712)
  - Analysis of 216,524 urinary bacterial isolates from Canadian long-term care residents (AMRNet pilot, 2016–2024) identified *Escherichia coli* in 51% of samples, with 44% non-susceptibility to fluoroquinolones and 18% to third-generation cephalosporins.
  - *Klebsiella pneumoniae* isolates demonstrated 56% non-susceptibility to nitrofurantoin, whereas carbapenem and aminoglycoside resistance remained consistently low across organisms.

- **Self-reported hypoglycemia highly prevalent among type 2 diabetes patients in Jordan** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366815)
  - A cross-sectional study of 326 adults with type 2 diabetes in northern Jordan found a 79.1% 6-month prevalence of self-reported hypoglycemia.
  - Independent risk factors included insulin use (aOR 3.27), sulfonylurea use (aOR 2.14), and diabetic nephropathy (aOR 3.76); 73.9% of participants were unaware that hypoglycemia can occur without symptoms, and 53.6% had never reported episodes to a provider.

- **Pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma outcomes limited by treatment abandonment in Ethiopia** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366799)
  - A retrospective cohort study of 94 pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma patients in Ethiopia demonstrated 1-year and 2-year overall survival (OS) rates of 70% and 42%, respectively.
  - Multivariable analysis identified treatment modality (p < 0.001) and total completed chemotherapy cycles (p = 0.001) as the primary independent determinants of overall survival.

- **Global survey maps adolescent depression and self-harm ideation across five LMICs** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.29.26366826)
  - Analysis of Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) data across 16,269 adolescents (aged 15–19) in Bangladesh, Lesotho, Mozambique, Nepal, and Zambia found a pooled probable depression prevalence of 3.9% and self-harm ideation prevalence of 7.0%.
  - Self-harm thoughts ranged from 3.1% in Zambia to 10.2% in Mozambique, with adolescent girls demonstrating higher rates than boys for both probable depression (4.9% vs 1.9%) and self-harm thoughts (8.6% vs 3.9%).

***

**Worth watching:** The methodological demonstration of data leakage shifts in medical AI models (e.g., SMOTE positioning altering held-out CKD diagnostic AUC from 0.939 to 0.604) highlights the strict validation protocols required before deploying machine learning diagnostic algorithms into clinical workflows.

- Economics
    - [What Anthropic’s IPO Filing Actually Says](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ic1Jf7VlXRM) -- Patrick Boyle
        - Anthropic filed an S-1 prospectus for a potential IPO targeting a valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.
        - The filing highlights an apparent $80 billion nominal loss alongside unexpected underlying operating profit, while its third-quarter growth rate quietly halved.
        - Financial footnotes reveal $800 billion in committed compute expenses buried in the filing.
        - The proposed corporate governance structure limits voting power, leaving ordinary shareholders with almost no input in company management.
        - Patrick Boyle analyzes whether Anthropic is a bubble or a bargain, concluding that current valuations rely heavily on speculation from both bulls and bears.
